input.quote: f) IBM agrees that, for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date of this Agreement, it will not in any way solicit for employment any Transferred Employees without the prior written consent of MSL
input.rationale: Section 9.0(f) imposes a one-way non-solicit on us (IBM). Scope is acceptable — it reaches only Transferred Employees (the personnel performing the outsourced work), it is a solicitation restriction rather than a no-hire, and it already carries the carve-outs our fallback requires for unsolicited approaches and general employment advertising/search firms. The material failure is duration: the restriction runs for "[*] years" from the Effective Date, i.e. plural years measured from signing rather than the 12 months from involvement contemplated by the fallback, and the redaction leaves open a period at or beyond the 24-month walk-away line. Because the transaction transfers our own employees to MSL, deleting the covenant outright (preferred position) is disproportionate, so we made the single minimal edit to bring the term to 12 months. We have not pressed for mutuality given the one-way nature of the employee transfer, but would accept a reciprocal formulation.

input.quote: f) IBM agrees that, for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date of this Agreement, it will not in any way solicit for employment any Transferred Employees without the prior written consent of MSL
input.rationale: Section 9.0(f) imposes a one-way non-solicit on us (IBM). Scope is acceptable — it reaches only Transferred Employees (the personnel performing the outsourced work), it is a solicitation restriction rather than a no-hire, and it already carries the carve-outs our fallback requires for unsolicited approaches and general employment advertising/search firms. The material failure is duration: the restriction runs for "[*] years" from the Effective Date, i.e. plural years measured from signing rather than the 12 months from involvement contemplated by the fallback, and the redaction leaves open a period at or beyond the 24-month walk-away line. Because the transaction transfers our own employees to MSL, deleting the covenant outright (preferred position) is disproportionate, so we made the single minimal edit to bring the term to 12 months. We have not pressed for mutuality given the one-way nature of the employee transfer, but would accept a reciprocal formulation.

paragraphs.text: 5.1 Breach
Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows:
Page 6 Dated 05/05/98
IBM Confidential

a) in the event of a material breach or default by the other Party of a material obligation of such Party under the Agreement which is not remedied within [*] Days after a written notice is given of such default or breach;
b) upon the occurrence of any of the following:
i) the other Party resolves to go into voluntary liquidation;
ii) a court orders the other Party to cease doing business;
iii) a receiver or administrative receiver is appointed over the whole or any part of the assets or property of the other Party;
iv) the other Party becomes unable to pay its debts because it is subject to a suspension of payments order, bankruptcy, or other insolvency proceeding; or
v) substantially all of the shares or assets of one Party are acquired by an entity that competes directly with the other Party.
In the case of i to v above, termination may also be effected by serving notice on the liquidator, administrator, acquirer, or receiver, as the case may be.

c) notice of the inability of the other Party to perform due to the existence of a Force Majeure event, as described in Section 16.17 of this Agreement, which is reasonably determined by the terminating Party to be a continuing condition.

Provided, however, that no such termination under this section after the Effective Date shall operate to rescind the transfer of the assets, as listed in Attachment 3: Asset List, unless IBM terminates this Agreement pursuant to Section 5.0 for MSL's failure to pay for such assets, in which case MSL shall return, at its cost, all such assets in MSL's possession at termination.
SECTION 4.0 TERM

This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of three (3) years unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0. This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement. Such renewals shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties.

The only MFN provision in the Agreement benefits us: at p1099, MSL agrees that MSL engineering "will be priced to IBM on a 'most favored customer' basis." That is a Vendor-granted MFN, which the playbook welcomes.

This sits at the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), so no edit is proposed.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant (preferred position).**

The agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on IBM. Purchases are purely order-driven — Section 6.0 makes IBM's purchase obligation subject to the agreement's terms with no requirements commitment, and Section 6.1 permits IBM to cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time. The only "exclusive" references are an entire-agreement clause and MSL's exclusive remedy under the loan agreement; the "solely" restrictions run against MSL (use of IBM Parts and purchased assets in IBM Products only), which benefits us. No redline proposed.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Vendor's home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad.

Find the governing-law clause; extract jurisdiction and dispute forum; note any arbitration seat.

Replace only the jurisdiction words and forum; keep the rest of the sentence intact.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

input.rationale: The agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binding IBM, which meets the preferred position (no restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build). I checked the sections most likely to carry such a covenant: § 6.0 Purchase of Products (p0720) creates only a purchase obligation for ordered Products with no requirements/exclusivity commitment; § 14.18 "Restrictions and Limitations" (p0995) and § 16.15 "Prohibited Suppliers" (p0319) restrict MSL, not IBM; and searches for "compete/competing/competitive", "exclusive", "sole/second source" and "IBM shall not" returned no restrictive covenant against us. The tangential hits are neutral or favourable to IBM: § 9.0(e) (p0186) expressly contemplates IBM reducing its Product requirements by migrating to a competitive supplier — confirming our freedom to dual-source; § 5.1(v) (p0116) is a mutual termination right on a change of control by a direct competitor; and the confidentiality agreement (p1491) preserves each party's freedom to provide competitive products and to supply the other's competitors. No redline is required.

content.text:
**Finding submitted — deviation (medium), § 9.0(f) / p0189.**

- **What it does:** One-way non-solicit binding us (IBM): for "[*] years" from the Effective Date we may not solicit Transferred Employees without MSL's written consent.
- **Compliant elements:** narrow scope (Transferred Employees only, not all MSL personnel), solicitation-only (no no-hire), and both fallback carve-outs already present (unsolicited self-initiated contact; general advertising/search firms).
- **Failure vs. fallback:** duration is expressed in plural "years" from signing rather than 12 months tied to involvement, and the redaction leaves open a period at or past the 24-month walk-away threshold.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** single edit narrowing the period to twelve (12) months; preferred deletion would be disproportionate here since the covenant protects the workforce we transferred to MSL.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

{"sectionRef":"§ 5.1 Breach","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0106","text":"5.1 Breach"},{"id":"p0107","text":"Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows:"},{"id":"p0108","text":"Page 6 Dated 05/05/98"},{"id":"p0109","text":"IBM Confidential"},{"id":"p0110","text":"a) in the event of a material breach or default by the other Party of a material obligation of such Party under the Agreement which is not remedied within [*] Days after a written notice is given of such default or breach;"},{"id":"p0111","text":"b) upon the occurrence of any of the following:"},{"id":"p0112","text":"i) the other Party resolves to go into voluntary liquidation;"},{"id":"p0113","text":"ii) a court orders the other Party to cease doing business;"},{"id":"p0114","text":"iii) a receiver or administrative receiver is appointed over the whole or any part of the assets or property of the other Party;"},{"id":"p0115","text":"iv) the other Party becomes unable to pay its debts because it is subject to a suspension of payments order, bankruptcy, or other insolvency proceeding; or"},{"id":"p0116","text":"v) substantially all of the shares or assets of one Party are acquired by an entity that competes directly with the other Party."},{"id":"p0117","text":"In the case of i to v above, termination may also be effected by serving notice on the liquidator, administrator, acquirer, or receiver, as the case may be."},{"id":"p0118","text":"c) notice of the inability of the other Party to perform due to the existence of a Force Majeure event, as described in Section 16.17 of this Agreement, which is reasonably determined by the terminating Party to be a continuing condition."},{"id":"p0119","text":"Provided, however, that no such termination under this section after the Effective Date shall operate to rescind the transfer of the assets, as listed in Attachment 3: Asset List, unless IBM terminates this Agreement pursuant to Section 5.0 for MSL's failure to pay for such assets, in which case MSL shall return, at its cost, all such assets in MSL's possession at termination."}]}

This purchase shall not include any Parts that are cancelable or otherwise transferable to IBM:"},{"id":"p0133","text":"ii) require delivery of all partially completed, and completed Products and inventory of purchased Parts, and buy them. This shall include Parts purchased and to be delivered to MSL to meet IBM's forecasted requirements, subject to the Supply flexibility set forth in Appendix 4 to the Statement of Work, but shall not include any Parts that are cancelable or otherwise transferable to IBM; or"},{"id":"p0134","text":"iii) require completion and delivery of any remaining units of Products on order as of the date of termination including inventory of purchased Parts and Parts purchased and to be delivered to MSL to meet IBM's forecasted requirements, subject to the Supply Flexibility set forth in Appendix 4 to the Statement of Work, but not including any Parts that are cancelable or otherwise transferable to IBM, and buy them, in which case MSL's obligations under 5.2 a) iii will be suspended until [*] Days after the appropriate Delivery Date."},{"id":"p0135","text":"c) Upon termination by MSL due to default by IBM, pursuant to Section 5.1 above, MSL shall complete Product(s) on order as of the date of termination, sell them to IBM, and deliver and sell to IBM Parts inventory. system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction on IBM, which satisfies the rule's *preferred* position outright (rather than merely the fallback).

What I checked:
- **§ 6.0 Purchase of Products (p0720)** — a plain obligation to purchase ordered Products; no requirements or exclusivity commitment, and it expressly does not authorise MSL to produce or deliver any Product.
- **§ 14.18 "Restrictions and Limitations" (p0995)** and **§ 16.15 "Prohibited Suppliers" (p0319)** — despite the promising headings, both bind MSL, not us. Per the detection guidance, restrictions on the vendor are acceptable.
- Targeted searches for "compete/competing/competitive", "exclusive", "sole/second source", "shall not manufacture" and "IBM shall not" surfaced no restrictive covenant against us.

The tangential hits are neutral or actively favourable to IBM, so I did not flag them:
- **§ 9.0(e) (p0186)** expressly contemplates IBM reducing its Product requirements "due to migration to a competitive supplier" — this confirms our freedom to dual-source and is a point in our favour.
- **§ 5.1(v) (p0116)** is a mutual change-of-control termination right, not a covenant.
- **AECI (p1491)** preserves each party's freedom to supply competitive products and to serve the other's competitors.

One drafting note, recorded here rather than as a deviation: because our purchase obligation is order-driven with no volume or requirements commitment, there is no latent de facto exclusivity to unwind. No action needed on this rule.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.
Severity: medium
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Position — fallback:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.
Position — walk-away:
Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.
Detection guidance:
"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

{"sectionRef":"§ 5.1 Breach","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0106","text":"5.1 Breach"},{"id":"p0107","text":"Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows:"},{"id":"p0108","text":"Page 6 Dated 05/05/98"},{"id":"p0109","text":"IBM Confidential"},{"id":"p0110","text":"a) in the event of a material breach or default by the other Party of a material obligation of such Party under the Agreement which is not remedied within [*] Days after a written notice is given of such default or breach;"},{"id":"p0111","text":"b) upon the occurrence of any of the following:"},{"id":"p0112","text":"i) the other Party resolves to go into voluntary liquidation;"},{"id":"p0113","text":"ii) a court orders the other Party to cease doing business;"},{"id":"p0114","text":"iii) a receiver or administrative receiver is appointed over the whole or any part of the assets or property of the other Party;"},{"id":"p0115","text":"iv) the other Party becomes unable to pay its debts because it is subject to a suspension of payments order, bankruptcy, or other insolvency proceeding; or"},{"id":"p0116","text":"v) substantially all of the shares or assets of one Party are acquired by an entity that competes directly with the other Party."},{"id":"p0117","text":"In the case of i to v above, termination may also be effected by serving notice on the liquidator, administrator, acquirer, or receiver, as the case may be."},{"id":"p0118","text":"c) notice of the inability of the other Party to perform due to the existence of a Force Majeure event, as described in Section 16.17 of this Agreement, which is reasonably determined by the terminating Party to be a continuing condition."},{"id":"p0119","text":"Provided, however, that no such termination under this section after the Effective Date shall operate to rescind the transfer of the assets, as listed in Attachment 3: Asset List, unless IBM terminates this Agreement pursuant to Section 5.0 for MSL's failure to pay for such assets, in which case MSL shall return, at its cost, all such assets in MSL's possession at termination."}]}

This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement. Such renewals shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties."}]}

{"sectionRef":"§ 5.2 Rights Upon Termination","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0120","text":"5.2 Rights Upon Termination"},{"id":"p0121","text":"a) Upon the expiration or termination for default of this Agreement, MSL will:"},{"id":"p0122","text":"i) within [*] Days after expiration or receipt of termination notice for default of this Agreement from IBM, cancel all Parts purchase orders, and within [*] Days, after such expiration or termination notice, prepare and submit to IBM a written inventory in reasonable detail of each of the following items in MSL's possession as of the date of termination:"},{"id":"p0123","text":"1. All Parts and partially completed Products. MSL shall continue to provide a detailed listing of Parts purchase order cancellations weekly until all issues are agreed to and resolved by the Parties."},{"id":"p0124","text":"2. All labeling and packaging material used for Products."},{"id":"p0125","text":"3. All completed Products covered by a Purchase Order not previously shipped to IBM."},{"id":"p0126","text":"Page 7 Dated 05/05/98"},{"id":"p0127","text":"IBM Confidential"},{"id":"p0128","text":"4. All IBM owned tooling."},{"id":"p0129","text":"ii) assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products as described in Attachment 1: Statement Of Work, to IBM or to another party that IBM designates."},{"id":"p0130","text":"iii) within [*] Days after expiration or termination of this Agreement, MSL shall return to IBM all copies of IBM Product documentation and all copies of any IBM confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media materials containing IBM confidential information of IBM."},{"id":"p0131","text":"b) Upon termination by IBM due to a default by MSL pursuant to Section 5.1 above, IBM shall, at its option, elect to do one of the following:"},{"id":"p0132","text":"i) be entitled to terminate all outstanding Purchase Orders without liability for such termination and purchase MSL's inventory of Parts, including Parts to be delivered to MSL to meet IBM's forecasted requirements, subject to the Supply Flexibility set forth in Appendix 4 to the Statement of Work. This purchase shall not include any Parts that are cancelable or otherwise transferable to IBM:"},{"id":"p0133","text":"ii) require delivery of all partially completed, and completed Products and inventory of purchased Parts, and buy them. This shall include Parts purchased and to be delivered to MSL to meet IBM's forecasted requirements, subject to the Supply flexibility set forth in Appendix 4 to the Statement of Work, but shall not include any Parts that are cancelable or otherwise transferable to IBM; or"},{"id":"p0134","text":"iii) require completion and delivery of any remaining units of Products on order as of the date of termination including inventory of purchased Parts and Parts purchased and to be delivered to MSL to meet IBM's forecasted requirements, subject to the Supply Flexibility set forth in Appendix 4 to the Statement of Work, but not including any Parts that are cancelable or otherwise transferable to IBM, and buy them, in which case MSL's obligations under 5.2 a) iii will be suspended until [*] Days after the appropriate Delivery Date."},{"id":"p0135","text":"c) Upon termination by MSL due to default by IBM, pursuant to Section 5.1 above, MSL shall complete Product(s) on order as of the date of termination, sell them to IBM, and deliver and sell to IBM Parts inventory. This shall include Parts purchased and to be delivered to MSL to meet IBM's forecasted requirements, subject to the Supply Flexibility set forth in Appendix 4 to the Statement of Work, but shall not include any Parts that are cancelable or otherwise transferable to IBM."}]}

input.quote: b) The total liability for either Party, regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort, is limited to three percent (3%) of the value of the bill of materials contained in the Products delivered to IBM and IBM Customers by MSL in the period beginning with the Effective Date of the Agreement through the resolution of the action.
input.rationale: Section 15.3 b) is the only monetary cap in the Base Agreement. It is mutual (good), and 15.3 a) contains a mutual consequential-damages waiver, but it fails the fallback on two material terms. First, the cap basis is 3% of the bill-of-materials value of all Products delivered over the whole term — a small fraction of the charges IBM pays MSL, and therefore materially below the fallback of twelve months' fees (and likely below six months' fees, i.e. walk-away territory). Second, there are no carve-outs anywhere: MSL's indemnity in 15.1 (third-party IP infringement, legal non-compliance, warranty failures), the confidentiality obligations in 13.2 and the AECI, gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside this cap with no super-cap, which the playbook treats as walk-away. The one-sided $25,000 limit in the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement §15 (p1574–p1575) caps MSL's remedies against IBM and benefits us, so we do not touch it. Redline resets the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' charges and US$1,000,000 and adds a single Excluded Claims sentence.

ops.oldText: is limited to three percent (3%) of the value of the bill of materials contained in the Products delivered to IBM and IBM Customers by MSL in the period beginning with the Effective Date of the Agreement through the resolution of the action.
ops.newText: is limited to the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by IBM to MSL under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the action and (b) one million U.S. dollars (US$1,000,000). This limitation does not apply to Excluded Claims, which means a Party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement, a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, a Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, a Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights, and IBM's obligation to pay amounts properly due under this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We reset the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' charges and US$1,000,000, because 3% of bill-of-materials value is well below our minimum of twelve months' fees. We also added the standard carve-outs so indemnification, confidentiality/security breaches, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, together with IBM's payment obligations.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.quote: b) The total liability for either Party, regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort, is limited to three percent (3%) of the value of the bill of materials contained in the Products delivered to IBM and IBM Customers by MSL in the period beginning with the Effective Date of the Agreement through the resolution of the action.
input.rationale: Section 15.3 b) is the only monetary cap in the Base Agreement. It is mutual (good), and 15.3 a) contains a mutual consequential-damages waiver, but it fails the fallback on two material terms. First, the cap basis is 3% of the bill-of-materials value of all Products delivered over the whole term — a small fraction of the charges IBM pays MSL, and therefore materially below the fallback of twelve months' fees (and likely below six months' fees, i.e. walk-away territory). Second, there are no carve-outs anywhere: MSL's indemnity in 15.1 (third-party IP infringement, legal non-compliance, warranty failures), the confidentiality obligations in 13.2 and the AECI, gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside this cap with no super-cap, which the playbook treats as walk-away. The one-sided $25,000 limit in the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement §15 (p1574–p1575) caps MSL's remedies against IBM and benefits us, so we do not touch it. Redline resets the mutual cap to the greater of twelve months' charges and US$1,000,000 and adds a single Excluded Claims sentence.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

elements.evidence: "IBM agrees that, for a period of twelve (12) months ... it will not in any way solicit for employment any Transferred Employees"

elements.element: Fallback: restriction is mutual (binds both Customer and Vendor)
elements.evidence: Only "IBM agrees that ... it will not in any way solicit"; no reciprocal MSL obligation appears.

elements.element: Fallback: carve-out for unsolicited approaches
elements.evidence: "employing any such person who contacts IBM on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from IBM"

elements.element: Fallback: no "no-hire" prohibition

reasons: The edit changes only the duration; the clause remains a one-way restriction on the Customer (IBM), so the fallback's express mutuality is absent.
Scope is still "any Transferred Employees" rather than personnel directly involved in the Services, so the population restricted is broader than the fallback permits.
The 12-month period runs "from the Effective Date of this Agreement" rather than from the end of each individual's involvement, which is the fallback trigger.
Carve-outs for unsolicited contact and general advertising, and the absence of any no-hire, are satisfied as drafted.

The change is narrowly scoped (a single duration operator) and introduces no undefined terms or dangling mechanics, so minimality and intent preservation are satisfied; however the fallback bargain is incomplete on mutuality, scope, and the duration trigger.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

Use the document tools for any needed source inspection. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. paragraphs.text: 16.2 Assignment

Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party. MSL may assign or subcontract all or any part of this Agreement to any MSL Related Company with IBM's prior written consent which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM. MSL shall
Page 19 Dated 05/05/98
IBM Confidential
provide IBM with all relevant details prior to implementing any change to its use of subcontractors performing work relating to IBM's Purchase Orders.
5.1 Breach
Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows:
Page 6 Dated 05/05/98
IBM Confidential

a) in the event of a material breach or default by the other Party of a material obligation of such Party under the Agreement which is not remedied within [*] Days after a written notice is given of such default or breach;
b) upon the occurrence of any of the following:
i) the other Party resolves to go into voluntary liquidation;
ii) a court orders the other Party to cease doing business;
iii) a receiver or administrative receiver is appointed over the whole or any part of the assets or property of the other Party;
iv) the other Party becomes unable to pay its debts because it is subject to a suspension of payments order, bankruptcy, or other insolvency proceeding; or
v) substantially all of the shares or assets of one Party are acquired by an entity that competes directly with the other Party.
In the case of i to v above, termination may also be effected by serving notice on the liquidator, administrator, acquirer, or receiver, as the case may be.

c) notice of the inability of the other Party to perform due to the existence of a Force Majeure event, as described in Section 16.17 of this Agreement, which is reasonably determined by the terminating Party to be a continuing condition.

Provided, however, that no such termination under this section after the Effective Date shall operate to rescind the transfer of the assets, as listed in Attachment 3: Asset List, unless IBM terminates this Agreement pursuant to Section 5.0 for MSL's failure to pay for such assets, in which case MSL shall return, at its cost, all such assets in MSL's possession at termination.

Parties: we represent International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); counterparty is Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL).

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.
